title: Oracle Pulled 50 Job Offers From IIT Students. India's Campuses Are Fighting Back.
excerpt: As the tech giant restructures around AI, students who secured prestigious Day 1 placements find themselves jobless — and IITs have blacklisted over 20 firms in response.
body:
The email arrived without warning. No call from a manager, no conversation with HR. Just a notification that the offer — secured after rounds of coding tests, system design interviews and the high-wire tension of IIT placement season — had been withdrawn.

More than 50 students across India's most prestigious engineering campuses received some version of that message in recent weeks, according to placement cell sources cited by The Economic Times. The affected institutions read like a roll call of Indian technical education's elite: IIT Delhi, IIT Kanpur, IIT Kharagpur, IIT Guwahati, IIT Madras, IIT BHU, IIT Hyderabad, IIT Roorkee, NIT Warangal and MNNIT Allahabad.

## The 'One Offer' Trap

The revocations are particularly devastating because of how IIT placement works. Under the system's strict "one-student-one-job" policy, once a student accepts an offer during placement season, they exit the pool entirely. They cannot interview with other companies. The policy exists to ensure fairness — preventing top students from hoarding multiple offers — but it also means that a revoked offer leaves a graduate with no backup and no institutional mechanism to re-enter the process.

Oracle had been an aggressive recruiter during the latest season, extending between 25 and 35 offers at some campuses for software engineering roles and internships. The company began withdrawing selected offers in recent weeks, affecting two to five students per institute.

For an IIT Bombay computer science graduate who spoke to Indian media, the experience was stark: an offer valued at nearly ₹30 lakh, withdrawn two days before his joining date. He was able to find an alternative through alumni networks. Many of his peers were not as fortunate.

## The AI Restructuring Behind the Cuts

Oracle's offer revocations are part of a much larger restructuring. The company is reportedly cutting between 10,000 and 30,000 roles globally as it pivots resources toward AI infrastructure and cloud computing — including a reported long-term cloud partnership with OpenAI valued at approximately $300 billion. In India alone, an estimated 12,000 employees have been affected, with cuts spanning cloud operations, healthcare divisions, sales teams and NetSuite units.

An affected Oracle employee, speaking to Firstpost anonymously, pushed back on the narrative that workers are being directly replaced by AI. The individual noted that AI tools had been in use within Oracle for years, primarily automating repetitive engineering tasks like validations, data processing and API integrations, while core logic development remained human-led. The layoffs, the employee argued, appeared to be strategic financial restructuring tied to Oracle's AI ambitions rather than performance-based decisions.

That distinction matters little to students whose offers have evaporated. The restructuring may be about capital reallocation rather than robot replacement, but the outcome is identical: fewer entry-level roles at a company that was, until weeks ago, among the most active recruiters on Indian campuses.

## The Campus Fightback

IITs have responded with an unprecedented collective action. The All IITs Placement Committee, coordinating across 15 campuses, has blacklisted over 20 firms — not just Oracle — from the 2025-26 placement season for revoking offers. The ban prevents these companies from participating in on-campus recruitment, though they can still hire through external channels.

The blacklist sends a signal, but it does not solve the immediate problem. Placement cells are reportedly expanding outreach to startups and companies under the government's Viksit Bharat initiative, trying to create alternative pathways for stranded graduates. The All India IT and ITeS Employees' Union (AIITEU) has gone further, calling Oracle's layoffs "illegal retrenchment" and demanding government intervention to enforce labour laws.

## The Pipeline Question

For the Indian diaspora — and for every family that has invested years and lakhs in engineering entrance preparation — the Oracle episode crystallises a structural anxiety. The traditional pathway (crack JEE → land Day 1 placement at a multinational → transfer to a US office → H-1B → green card) has been the aspirational conveyor belt for a generation. When a company as established as Oracle can retract 50 offers in a single cycle, the conveyor belt looks considerably less reliable.

The broader pattern is clear: AI is not just changing what engineers build. It is changing how many engineers companies believe they need, and where those engineers sit. For India's campus placement system — designed for an era of predictable multinational hiring — the reckoning is just beginning.
